summary.plain: The nuclear-physics institute of Mainz University in Germany operates MAMI, an electron microtron delivering precise electron beams up to 1.5 GeV for hadron-structure experiments (A1, A2), and is building the new MESA accelerator for precision electroweak and dark-sector experiments.
summary.technical: Institut für Kernphysik, JGU Mainz (more than 150 employees): MAMI (racetrack and harmonic double-sided microtrons, 855 MeV and 1.5 GeV) with the A1 spectrometer and A2 Crystal Ball/TAPS halls; MESA energy-recovering superconducting linac (up to 155 MeV, 10 mA) under construction with P2, MAGIX and DarkMESA, within the PRISMA+ cluster of excellence.
